title: Traffic-aware sampled evals for catalog and tenant upgrades
creator: Lena Torres
description: Problem: When a model version is pinned or upgraded (catalog-wide or tenant-specific), we run preflight tests but usually on either synthetic corpora or a coarse tenant sample. That can miss regressions that only surface under real traffic distributions or hot prompt slices. This ticket proposes a traffic-aware sampled evaluation system that automatically picks a small but representative set of tenants and traffic slices to exercise on every pin/upgrade, combining lightweight synthetic checks with short live-traffic replay and differential scoring. Goals: reduce undetected regressions, provide faster signal for rollback decisions, and keep eval cost bounded by adapting sample size to traffic and risk profile.
motivation: Current preflight pipelines produce too many false negatives for tenant-specific regressions. Large customers with unique prompt distributions have historically been the source of surprise regressions after catalog promotions. By making the eval trigger aware of traffic patterns and tenant risk, we can allocate eval budget more effectively and generate high-confidence signals for canary decisions and automated rollbacks.
proposed_solution: 1) On a pin/upgrade event, fetch recent 7-day traffic metadata for affected tenants and the catalog model (traffic volume, avg token length, common endpoints). 2) Score tenants by risk (traffic volume x novelty of prompts x SLA tier). 3) Select a top-k sample of tenants (k configurable; default 5) plus a set of synthetic probes covering edge prompt classes. 4) For each selected tenant: run a short live-traffic replay (rate-limited), and run synthetic hypothesis tests (fidelity and safety metrics). 5) Compute differential metrics vs. baseline pinned-version: statistical significance, quality deltas per route and prompt slice, and a composite impact score. 6) Emit a pass/fail + detailed report; if impact score exceeds configured thresholds for the tenant or catalog, mark event for manual review or trigger automated rollback policy. 7) Integrate report into Console rollout UI and event logs for audits.
acceptance_criteria: Traffic fetch job returns tenant-level metadata for 7-day window for >=95% of active tenants
Risk-scoring algorithm implemented and tested with synthetic workloads
Sampling UI + API accepts a pin event and returns chosen tenants within 5 minutes
Live-traffic replay executes at safe rates (configurable) and cannot exceed tenant quota/SLAs
Differential scoring computes per-route quality deltas and a composite impact score
Rollout decision output emitted in machine-readable format and visible in Console
End-to-end run cost remains below $X (configurable budget) for default sample sizes
runbook_snippet: If a pin-run returns composite impact score >= critical_threshold: 1) Halt rollout; notify on-call PM and SRE. 2) Attach full diff report to the pin-event. 3) If automated rollback enabled, execute rollback policy and create ENG incident ticket with diagnostics. For non-critical but medium impact: schedule focused canary with increased sampling for next 24 hours.
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: Live-traffic replay could expose production data to eval pipelines. Mitigation: replay in-tenant only (no cross-tenant aggregation), strip PII via existing sanitizers, and run under tenant consent flags for private deployments. Risk: Added latency to promotion pipelines. Mitigation: make sampling asynchronous and emit a provisional pass if quick synthetic checks pass; full verdict can retroactively halt if regressions are found.
metrics: % of upgrades flagged for manual review (expected decrease)
Mean time to rollback for detected regressions
False negative rate against historical incident set
notes: We should coordinate with Privacy and Legal for replay consent on private deployments. Also align with SRE on safe rate limits and Circuit Breaker hooks. This complements, not replaces, existing preflight/verifier systems documented in the catalog eval playbook.
